title: Implement multi-pattern string search in Python
description: Implement find_all(text, patterns) that returns all (start, pattern) matches in text for any pattern in patterns. Uses a simple approach (not full Aho-Corasick): iterate each pattern, scan text.

files.tests/test_search.py:
from src.search import find_all

def test_single_pattern():
    result = find_all('hello world', ['world'])
    assert result == [(6, 'world')]

def test_multiple_patterns():
    result = find_all('abcabc', ['abc', 'bc'])
    # abc at 0, 3; bc at 1, 4 — sorted by start
    assert result == [(0, 'abc'), (1, 'bc'), (3, 'abc'), (4, 'bc')]

def test_overlapping():
    result = find_all('aaaa', ['aa'])
    assert result == [(0, 'aa'), (1, 'aa'), (2, 'aa')]

def test_no_match():
    result = find_all('hello', ['xyz'])
    assert result == []

def test_empty_text():
    result = find_all('', ['abc'])
    assert result == []

- At each position check text[i:i+len(pattern)] == pattern; if so, append (i, pattern)
- Collect all matches across all patterns, sort by (start, pattern), deduplicate, return
